brief: GS's Q3 2026 earnings preview: consensus expects 27% y/y S&P 500 EPS growth, a deceleration from Q2's 33% but the highest pre-season estimate since 2021. GS expects another quarter of beats because neither macro data nor AI-investment signals point to a slowdown. Info Tech and Energy drive ~80% of growth (median stock up >30% in each), while consumer sectors show no aggregate growth; Micron and Nvidia alone contribute over a third of index growth, and Micron already beat with 1,003% y/y earnings growth. Market breadth is at its narrowest since the Dot Com Bubble even as the index sits 2% from its high. Hyperscaler capex growth (116% vs 87% in Q2) and accelerating cloud revenue (48% to an expected 55%) remain the AI-monetization engine. Last quarter's ~$150bn equity-stake "other income" boost (12% of EPS) should fade in Q3, while tariff refunds (~$69bn, 6% of pre-tax profits) keep providing a modest offset. Margins are expected to hold near 14.7% but with slight sequential compression from input costs.
